## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code diagnoses a BERT4Rec model through a compatibility view; the backbone implementation is not included. It reads real-item embeddings from `view.item_emb.weight[1:itemnum+1]`, excluding padding and the reserved mask token. Sequence representations come from `view.log2feats(sequence)` and are scored through `view.predict_score(features, items)`.

The probe uses features at every valid target position, rather than explicitly computing a final user representation. Correct masked-target handling and final-nonpadding readout must therefore be implemented by the underlying model/view; this file does not verify them.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the view and its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Reviews and histories are retained but not directly analyzed. The view exposes the actual network as `view.model`.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` examines up to ten batches shaped `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, with sequence and target tensors of shape B × L. It switches to evaluation mode, disables gradients, computes sequence features, and scores paired positive/negative items at each position. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result to [0,1]. Higher values indicate stronger directional alignment; approximately 0.5 indicates near-zero average cosine similarity.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Computes positive logit minus negative logit. Higher mean and 10th-percentile margins suggest clearer separation. Lower negative-beats-positive and margin-below-0.5 rates are preferable.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts positive and negative item categories among weak-margin and incorrectly ranked positions, retaining the top 20 categories. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so these lists should be empty; counts alone do not measure normalized category difficulty.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence perturbation, shuffle, ablation, gradient analysis, or SVD is performed. Random embedding subsampling and sampled-negative comparisons are the only sampling-based checks.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The returned dictionary contains `metrics` and matching `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)` embeds both into instructions for a separate JSON interpretation containing status, findings, implications, and evidence.

These training-batch diagnostics do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking quality, sequence sensitivity, or target leakage. Empty valid-target batches produce zero margin metrics, which can misleadingly resemble healthy error rates.

Recent work distinguishes item relatedness from evidence of compatibility. [ECCR (2024)](https://www.amazon.science/publications/eccr-explainable-and-coherent-complement-recommendation-based-on-large-language-models) argues that co-purchase alone does not establish whether products work together. This motivates contrastive audit pairs: a broadly similar candidate versus one with explicit title/description evidence of compatible model, format, dimensions, or purpose. Record supporting text and missing specifications; distinguish substitutes, complements, and possible redundancy without assuming previous interactions imply ownership. These are proposed audit rules, not established findings about the twenty users.

Temporal recommendation research supports examining recent and older evidence separately. [ICMA (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.222/) models temporal variability and long-term dependencies; [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) distinguishes interaction timing beyond sequence order. Useful probes therefore compare recent-interest matches against older recurring interests, recording timestamps and repeated support. Neither recency nor similarity establishes present intent, mood, or immediate need. Treat those interpretations as hypotheses requiring feedback.

For the twenty-user audit, collect pairwise preference, supporting reason, and “cannot assess” responses. Report assessable-pair coverage, compatibility preference, redundancy objections, and recent-versus-older preference with explicit denominators; keep these separate from validation HR@10. Unidentified items or missing compatibility evidence should remain unassessable. [Conformal abstention research (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.01563) supports abstention under uncertainty in question answering, but does not validate this recommendation audit. Likewise, [user-centric explanation research (2024)](https://aamas.csc.liv.ac.uk/Proceedings/aamas2024/pdfs/p2174.pdf) indicates explanation effectiveness can vary by user: validate interpretations against actual feedback rather than persuasive wording or invented attributes.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code diagnoses a BERT4Rec model through a compatibility view; the backbone implementation is not included. It reads real-item embeddings from `view.item_emb.weight[1:itemnum+1]`, excluding padding and the reserved mask token. Sequence representations come from `view.log2feats(sequence)` and are scored through `view.predict_score(features, items)`.

The probe uses features at every valid target position, rather than explicitly computing a final user representation. Correct masked-target handling and final-nonpadding readout must therefore be implemented by the underlying model/view; this file does not verify them.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the view and its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Reviews and histories are retained but not directly analyzed. The view exposes the actual network as `view.model`.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` examines up to ten batches shaped `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, with sequence and target tensors of shape B × L. It switches to evaluation mode, disables gradients, computes sequence features, and scores paired positive/negative items at each position. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result to [0,1]. Higher values indicate stronger directional alignment; approximately 0.5 indicates near-zero average cosine similarity.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Computes positive logit minus negative logit. Higher mean and 10th-percentile margins suggest clearer separation. Lower negative-beats-positive and margin-below-0.5 rates are preferable.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts positive and negative item categories among weak-margin and incorrectly ranked positions, retaining the top 20 categories. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so these lists should be empty; counts alone do not measure normalized category difficulty.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence perturbation, shuffle, ablation, gradient analysis, or SVD is performed. Random embedding subsampling and sampled-negative comparisons are the only sampling-based checks.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The returned dictionary contains `metrics` and matching `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)` embeds both into instructions for a separate JSON interpretation containing status, findings, implications, and evidence.

These training-batch diagnostics do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking quality, sequence sensitivity, or target leakage. Empty valid-target batches produce zero margin metrics, which can misleadingly resemble healthy error rates.
